claim: The standard reference Caenorhabditis elegans strain, N2, has evolved marked behavioral changes in social feeding behavior since its isolation from the wild.
source: The standard reference Caenorhabditis elegans strain, N2, has evolved marked behavioral changes in social feeding behavior since its isolation from the wild.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: The causal, laboratory-derived mutations in two genes, npr-1 and glb-5, confer large fitness advantages in standard laboratory conditions.
source: We show that the causal, laboratory-derived mutations in two genes, npr-1 and glb-5, confer large fitness advantages in standard laboratory conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by competition experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The fitness advantages of the derived alleles remained unchanged when social/solitary behavior differences were suppressed using environmental manipulations.
source: Using environmental manipulations that suppress social/solitary behavior differences, we show the fitness advantages of the derived alleles remained unchanged, suggesting selection on these alleles acted through pleiotropic traits.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through experiments in Figure 3.

claim: N2 animals mature faster than a strain containing ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5.
source: Transcriptomics, developmental timing, and food consumption assays showed that N2 animals mature faster, produce more sperm, and consume more food than a strain containing ancestral alleles of these genes regardless of behavioral strategies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5e and 5i.

claim: N2 animals produce more sperm than a strain containing ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5.
source: Transcriptomics, developmental timing, and food consumption assays showed that N2 animals mature faster, produce more sperm, and consume more food than a strain containing ancestral alleles of these genes regardless of behavioral strategies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5f.

claim: N2 animals consume more food than a strain containing ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5.
source: Transcriptomics, developmental timing, and food consumption assays showed that N2 animals mature faster, produce more sperm, and consume more food than a strain containing ancestral alleles of these genes regardless of behavioral strategies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6b and 6d.

claim: The pleiotropic effects of glb-5 and npr-1 are a consequence of changes to O2-sensing neurons that regulate both aerotaxis and energy homeostasis.
source: Our data suggest that the pleiotropic effects of glb-5 and npr-1 are a consequence of changes to O2 -sensing neurons that regulate both aerotaxis and energy homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with URX neuron ablation in Figure 7.

claim: The N2 strain was isolated by L.N. Staniland and Warwick Nicholas from mushroom compost in 1951.
source: While this strain was introduced to the genetics research community by Sydney Brenner in 1974 (Brenner, 1974), it was actually isolated by L.N. Staniland and Warwick Nicholas from mushroom compost in 1951, spending multiple decades (~300–2000 generations) in two primary growth conditions: on agar plates where bacteria was its primary food source or in liquid axenic media (Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Sterken et al., 2015.

claim: The N2 strain spent multiple decades (~300–2000 generations) in two primary growth conditions: on agar plates where bacteria was its primary food source or in liquid axenic media.
source: While this strain was introduced to the genetics research community by Sydney Brenner in 1974 (Brenner, 1974), it was actually isolated by L.N. Staniland and Warwick Nicholas from mushroom compost in 1951, spending multiple decades (~300–2000 generations) in two primary growth conditions: on agar plates where bacteria was its primary food source or in liquid axenic media (Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Sterken et al., 2015.

claim: A neomorphic, missense mutation in the neuropeptide receptor gene npr-1 arose and fixed in the N2 strain following isolation from the wild.
source: A small number (~100) of new mutations that arose and fixed in the N2 strain following isolation from the wild have been identified (McGrath et al., 2011), including a neomorphic, missense mutation in the neuropeptide receptor gene npr-1 and a recessive, 765 bp duplication in the nematode-specific globin gene glb-5.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to McGrath et al., 2011.

claim: A recessive, 765 bp duplication in the nematode-specific globin gene glb-5 arose and fixed in the N2 strain following isolation from the wild.
source: A small number (~100) of new mutations that arose and fixed in the N2 strain following isolation from the wild have been identified (McGrath et al., 2011), including a neomorphic, missense mutation in the neuropeptide receptor gene npr-1 and a recessive, 765 bp duplication in the nematode-specific globin gene glb-5.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to McGrath et al., 2011.

claim: npr-1 and glb-5 mutations were originally identified for their role in foraging and aerotaxis behaviors.
source: These mutations were originally identified for their role in foraging and aerotaxis behaviors and were initially thought to represent natural genetic variants (de Bono and Bargmann, 1998; Persson et al., 2009) (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to de Bono and Bargmann, 1998 and Persson et al., 2009.

claim: npr-1 and glb-5 regulate the activity of the URX-RMG neuronal circuit that controls O2 responses on food.
source: A large body of work has found that these genes regulate the activity of the URX-RMG neuronal circuit that controls O2 responses on food (Chang et al., 2006; Coates and de Bono, 2002; Gray et al., 2004; Macosko et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2009; Persson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Animals with the ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 prefer ~10% O2 concentrations while foraging and follow O2 gradients to the border of bacterial lawns (~12% O2) and feed in groups (called social behavior).
source: Animals with the ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 prefer ~10% O2 concentrations while foraging and follow O2 gradients to the border of bacterial lawns (~12% O2) and feed in groups (called social behavior); animals containing the derived alleles of these genes are less sensitive to 10–21% O2 gradients in the presence of food and feed alone (called solitary behavior) (Chang and Bargmann, 2008; Chang et al., 2006; Gray et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Chang and Bargmann, 2008; Chang et al., 2006; Gray et al., 2004.

claim: Animals containing the derived alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 are less sensitive to 10–21% O2 gradients in the presence of food and feed alone (called solitary behavior).
source: Animals with the ancestral alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 prefer ~10% O2 concentrations while foraging and follow O2 gradients to the border of bacterial lawns (~12% O2) and feed in groups (called social behavior); animals containing the derived alleles of these genes are less sensitive to 10–21% O2 gradients in the presence of food and feed alone (called solitary behavior) (Chang and Bargmann, 2008; Chang et al., 2006; Gray et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Chang and Bargmann, 2008; Chang et al., 2006; Gray et al., 2004.

claim: The derived alleles of glb-5 and npr-1 were fixed by selection as solitary animals are more likely to be picked when propagating animals to new plates.
source: We have previously proposed that the derived alleles of glb-5 and npr-1 were fixed by selection as solitary animals are more likely to be picked when propagating animals to new plates (McGrath et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a hypothesis previously proposed by the authors, cited to McGrath et al., 2009.

claim: Aggregation behavior in the ancestral npr-1 strain appears to create local food depletion leading to a weak starvation state, which reduces reproduction and growth.
source: However, aggregation behavior in the ancestral npr-1 strain appears to create local food depletion leading to a weak starvation state, which reduces reproduction and growth (Andersen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Andersen et al., 2014.

claim: Experimental crosses or competition experiments between parental strains that are polymorphic for npr-1 have resulted in enrichment of the derived allele of npr-1.
source: Consistent with both hypotheses, a number of experimental crosses or competition experiments between parental strains that are polymorphic for npr-1 have resulted in enrichment of the derived allele of npr-1, suggesting it confers a fitness advantage under standard lab husbandry (Gloria-Soria and Azevedo, 2008; Noble et al., 2017; Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Gloria-Soria and Azevedo, 2008; Noble et al., 2017; Weber et al., 2010.

claim: The derived allele of npr-1 confers a fitness advantage under standard lab husbandry.
source: Consistent with both hypotheses, a number of experimental crosses or competition experiments between parental strains that are polymorphic for npr-1 have resulted in enrichment of the derived allele of npr-1, suggesting it confers a fitness advantage under standard lab husbandry (Gloria-Soria and Azevedo, 2008; Noble et al., 2017; Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Gloria-Soria and Azevedo, 2008; Noble et al., 2017; Weber et al., 2010.

claim: The derived alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 suppress bordering behavior to varying degrees.
source: We confirmed previous reports that both the derived alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 suppress bordering behavior to varying degrees (Bendesky et al., 2012; de Bono and Bargmann, 1998; McGrath et al., 2009); npr-1 accounted for the majority of the difference with glb-5 playing a modulatory role (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Bendesky et al., 2012; de Bono and Bargmann, 1998; McGrath et al., 2009, and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: npr-1 accounted for the majority of the difference in bordering behavior with glb-5 playing a modulatory role.
source: We confirmed previous reports that both the derived alleles of npr-1 and glb-5 suppress bordering behavior to varying degrees (Bendesky et al., 2012; de Bono and Bargmann, 1998; McGrath et al., 2009); npr-1 accounted for the majority of the difference with glb-5 playing a modulatory role (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: The N2 strain was the most fit in laboratory conditions with a relative fitness (w) of ~1.30.
source: The N2 strain was the most fit in these conditions, with a relative fitness (w) of ~1.30.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: The fitness effects of the glb-5 and npr-1 regions were epistatic.
source: Interestingly, the fitness effects of the glb-5 and npr-1 regions were epistatic - the derived allele of glb-5 increased the relative fitness in the derived npr-1 background but showed no effect in the ancestral allele of npr-1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: The derived allele of glb-5 increased the relative fitness in the derived npr-1 background but showed no effect in the ancestral allele of npr-1.
source: Interestingly, the fitness effects of the glb-5 and npr-1 regions were epistatic - the derived allele of glb-5 increased the relative fitness in the derived npr-1 background but showed no effect in the ancestral allele of npr-1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: The derived npr-1 allele increased fitness in both backgrounds of glb-5.
source: The derived npr-1 allele increased fitness in both backgrounds of glb-5.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: The estimated selective coefficient of the glb-5 allele in the npr-1 derived background was s = 0.10 (0.06–0.13 95% confidence interval).
source: The estimated selective coefficient (a common measure of the fitness difference of a beneficial allele) of the glb-5 allele in the npr-1 derived background was s = 0.10 (0.06–0.13 95% confidence interval), the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 ancestral background was s = 0.17 (0.12–0.23 95% confidence interval), and the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 derived background was s = 0.30 (0.27–0.34 95% confidence interval).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments.

claim: The estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 ancestral background was s = 0.17 (0.12–0.23 95% confidence interval).
source: The estimated selective coefficient (a common measure of the fitness difference of a beneficial allele) of the glb-5 allele in the npr-1 derived background was s = 0.10 (0.06–0.13 95% confidence interval), the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 ancestral background was s = 0.17 (0.12–0.23 95% confidence interval), and the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 derived background was s = 0.30 (0.27–0.34 95% confidence interval).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments.

claim: The estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 derived background was s = 0.30 (0.27–0.34 95% confidence interval).
source: The estimated selective coefficient (a common measure of the fitness difference of a beneficial allele) of the glb-5 allele in the npr-1 derived background was s = 0.10 (0.06–0.13 95% confidence interval), the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 ancestral background was s = 0.17 (0.12–0.23 95% confidence interval), and the estimated selective coefficient of the npr-1 allele in the glb-5 derived background was s = 0.30 (0.27–0.34 95% confidence interval).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments.

claim: These selective coefficients are comparable to beneficial alleles identified in other organisms, such as the haplotype responsible for lactase persistence (~0.01–0.19) and the sickle-cell trait (0.05–0.18) in humans.
source: These selective coefficients are comparable to beneficial alleles identified in other organisms, such as the haplotype responsible for lactase persistence (~0.01–0.19) (Bersaglieri et al., 2004) and the sickle-cell trait (0.05–0.18) in humans (Li, 1975).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Bersaglieri et al., 2004 and Li, 1975.

claim: Both the npr-1(ad609) and npr-1(ky13) loss-of-function alleles decreased the animal's relative fitness in an amount comparable to the ancestral allele.
source: Both the npr-1(ad609) and npr-1(ky13) loss-of-function alleles decreased the animal's relative fitness in an amount comparable to the ancestral allele (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2c.

claim: Bordering behavior differences between N2glb-5, npr-1 and N2 can be suppressed by reducing environmental O2 levels to 10% or 3%.
source: We first confirmed that we could suppress the bordering behavior differences between N2glb-5, npr-1 and N2 by reducing environmental O2 levels to 10% or 3% using a Biospherix chamber (Figure 3a and Videos 1–4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3a and Videos 1-4.

claim: N2glb-5, npr-1 animals did not form any social groups in the center of the lawn at the lowered O2 levels and were also indistinguishable from N2 by visual inspection.
source: N2glb-5, npr-1 animals did not form any social groups in the center of the lawn at the lowered O2 levels and were also indistinguishable from N2 by visual inspection.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on visual observations.

claim: O2 manipulation suppressed roaming/dwelling behavior differences between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1.
source: We also verified that this O2 manipulation also suppressed roaming/dwelling behavior (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3b.

claim: Animals that are mutant for npr-1 show increased amounts of roaming behavior.
source: While feeding, C. elegans worms alternate between bouts of active exploration (roaming) and periods of inactive movement (dwelling). Animals that are mutant for npr-1 show increased amounts of roaming behavior (Stern et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Stern et al., 2017.

claim: The relative fitness differences between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 strains remained unchanged at lower O2 levels despite behavioral similarity.
source: Despite the behavioral similarity of these animals at these lower O2 levels, the relative fitness differences between the N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 strains remained (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3c.

claim: Uniform bacterial lawns (UBLs) were unable to suppress the fitness advantage of N2 animals.
source: UBLs have been used to suppress npr-1-dependent differences in survival in response to bacterial pathogens (Reddy et al., 2009); however, the UBLs were unable to suppress the fitness advantage of N2 animals (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Reddy et al., 2009, and supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: Animals that carry the ancestral npr-1 allele can burrow into agar when food is depleted.
source: Animals that carry the ancestral npr-1 allele can burrow into agar when food is depleted (de Bono and Bargmann, 1998), raising the possibility that the fitness gains of N2 could be a result of the transfer process, which selects for animals on the surface of plates.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to de Bono and Bargmann, 1998.

claim: The relative fitness differences between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 remained unchanged on agarose plates that prevent burrowing.
source: While visual inspection of the two strains at 10% and 3% did not reveal any obvious differences in burrowing behavior, we also tested the role of burrowing in the fitness differences more rigorously by using modified nematode growth plates that contain agarose that prevents burrowing (Andersen et al., 2014). The relative fitness differences between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 remained unchanged (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Andersen et al., 2014, and supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: Both glb-5 and npr-1 have been implicated in innate immunity and survival to pathogen exposure.
source: Both glb-5 and npr-1 have been implicated in innate immunity and survival to pathogen exposure (Andersen et al., 2014; Reddy et al., 2009; Styer et al., 2008; Zuckerman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Andersen et al., 2014; Reddy et al., 2009; Styer et al., 2008; Zuckerman et al., 2017.

claim: The fitness advantage of the N2 strain compared to the N2glb-5, npr-1 strain remained when animals were competed against each other on OP50 bacteria killed by ultraviolet radiation.
source: However, the fitness advantage of the N2 strain compared to the N2glb-5, npr-1 strain remained when animals were competed against each other on OP50 bacteria killed by ultraviolet radiation (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3e.

claim: The relative fitness on killed OP50 bacteria was slightly decreased compared to live bacteria.
source: The relative fitness on killed OP50 bacteria was slightly decreased; however, this could reflect differences in population demographics, as the killed OP50 supported less overall growth per plate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on observations from experiments.

claim: Eleven wild strains isolated from different parts of the world all aggregated at the borders of the bacterial lawn, consistent with their npr-1 genotype.
source: Consistent with their npr-1 genotype, these wild strains all aggregated at the borders of the bacterial lawn (Figure 4a), but their relative fitness differences varied wildly (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4a.

claim: The relative fitness of wild strains varied wildly despite similar bordering behavior.
source: Consistent with their npr-1 genotype, these wild strains all aggregated at the borders of the bacterial lawn (Figure 4a), but their relative fitness differences varied wildly (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4b.

claim: The relative fitness of two wild strains (CB4856 and DL238) was greatly reduced compared to the N2glb-5, npr-1 strain.
source: The relative fitness of two of the strains (CB4856 and DL238) was greatly reduced compared to the N2glb-5, npr-1 strain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The relative fitness of five wild strains were comparable to the N2.
source: The relative fitness of five of the strains were comparable to the N2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The relative fitness of four wild strains was statistically indistinguishable from the barcoded N2glb-5, npr-1.
source: The relative fitness of the remaining four strains was statistically indistinguishable from the barcoded N2glb-5, npr-1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Social behavior is not the major determinant of fitness levels in laboratory conditions.
source: These results further support that social behavior is not the major determinant of fitness levels in laboratory conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the wild strain experiments.

claim: The PCA analysis identified a single component that explained the majority of the variance (77.9%) in transcriptional profiles.
source: However, the PCA analysis identified a single component that explained the majority of the variance (77.9%).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on PCA analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Reducing O2 levels from 21% to 10% had similar effects on the transcription profiles as changing the background from N2glb-5, npr-1 to N2.
source: Reducing O2 levels from 21% to 10% had similar effects on the transcription profiles as changing the background from N2glb-5, npr-1 to N2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on PCA analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The animals that differed in both genetic background and environmental O2 levels (N2–21% O2 vs N2glb-5, npr-1–10% O2) showed the most similar transcriptional profiles.
source: Consequently, the animals that differed in both genetic background and environmental O2 levels (N2–21% O2 vs N2glb-5, npr-1–10% O2) also showed the most similar transcriptional profiles.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on PCA analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The foraging behavioral differences are not responsible for the underlying transcriptomics differences between the different strains and environmental conditions.
source: These results suggest that the foraging behavioral differences are not responsible for the underlying transcriptomics differences between the different strains and environmental conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the transcriptomics analysis.

claim: A cluster of 652 genes showed identical effects on transcription for both environmental and genetic perturbations.
source: Surprisingly, we observed a bimodal distribution of values, with a cluster of 652 genes centered at 1.2 log2-fold change (Figure 5c – red circle). This is unexpected, as it suggests that the environmental and genetic perturbations had identical effects on transcription for all these genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5c.

claim: A large number of genes in the 652 gene cluster are known to be involved in spermatogenesis.
source: When we inspected this list of genes, we noticed a large number of genes that are known to be involved in spermatogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on analysis of the gene cluster.

claim: The expression of the majority of the 652 genes peaked during the L4 stage in hermaphrodites, was further enriched in L4 males, and suppressed in somatic cells isolated from L4 animals.
source: The expression of the majority of these genes peaked during the L4 stage in hermaphrodites, was further enriched in L4 males, and suppressed in somatic cells isolated from L4 animals.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on analysis using previously published transcriptomics data (Boeck et al., 2016), shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The 652 gene cluster is enriched in germline cells and consistent with involvement in spermatogenesis.
source: These observations are consistent with this cluster of genes being involved in spermatogenesis, which occurs during the L4 stage (when RNA was isolated) in hermaphrodite animals.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the expression patterns.

claim: N2 animals began spermatogenesis approximately 2 hr earlier than the N2glb-5, npr-1 animals, regardless of the environmental O2 levels.
source: N2 animals began spermatogenesis approximately 2 hr earlier than the N2glb-5, npr-1 animals, regardless of the environmental O2 levels (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5e.

claim: Hermaphrodites undergo spermatogenesis for a fixed period of time before permanently switching gametogenesis to the production of oocytes, resulting in the development of a fixed number of self-sperm that are stored in the spermathecae.
source: Hermaphrodites undergo spermatogenesis for a fixed period of time before permanently switching gametogenesis to the production of oocytes, resulting in the development of a fixed number of self-sperm that are stored in the spermathecae (Hubbard and Greenstein, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Hubbard and Greenstein, 2005.

claim: N2 animals produced more sperm than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals.
source: Not only did N2 animals start spermatogenesis earlier, they also produced more sperm (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5f.

claim: The total fecundity of N2 hermaphrodites that do not mate with males is determined by the number of self-sperm.
source: The total fecundity of N2 hermaphrodites that do not mate with males is determined by the number of self-sperm.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as established knowledge.

claim: The difference in self-sperm number resulted in a larger overall brood size in N2 animals.
source: We confirmed that the difference in self-sperm number also resulted in a larger overall brood size (Figure 5g) and as expected from computational modeling (Large et al., 2017), an increased rate of egg-laying later on in life (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5g.

claim: N2 animals showed an increased rate of egg-laying later on in life compared to N2glb-5, npr-1 animals.
source: We confirmed that the difference in self-sperm number also resulted in a larger overall brood size (Figure 5g) and as expected from computational modeling (Large et al., 2017), an increased rate of egg-laying later on in life (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Large et al., 2017, and supported by data in Figure 5h.

claim: N2 animals were observed to contain fertilized eggs approximately 1 hr earlier than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals.
source: Again, we observed a difference in N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 animals at both 10% and 21% environmental O2 levels. N2 animals were observed to contain fertilized eggs approximately 1 hr earlier that N2glb-5, npr-1 animals (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5i.

claim: The differences in transcription between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 could be caused by differences in sexual maturity.
source: These experiments suggest that the differences in transcription between N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 could be caused by differences in sexual maturity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the timing experiments.

claim: The rate of spermatogenesis or expression levels of genes may be modified by O2 levels that are not reflected in the timing of the presence of mature sperm.
source: Potentially, the rate of spermatogenesis or expression levels of genes are modified by O2 levels that are not reflected in the timing of the presence of mature sperm.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a speculation to explain observations.

claim: N2 animals were larger than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals at synchronized time points.
source: We measured the size of N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 animals and found that N2 animals were also larger than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals at synchronized time points (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6a.

claim: The N2 strain seems to violate life-history tradeoffs, as it sexually matures earlier than N2glb-5, npr-1, but also produces more eggs later on in life.
source: The N2 strain seems to violate this tradeoff, as it sexually matures earlier than N2glb-5, npr-1, but also produces more eggs later on in life.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation that contradicts expected tradeoffs.

claim: Metabolism genes were upregulated by the derived npr-1 allele, which was proposed to represent differences in food intake.
source: This would be consistent with Andersen et al's observation that metabolism genes were upregulated by the derived npr-1 allele, which they proposed represented differences in food intake (Andersen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Andersen et al., 2014.

claim: npr-1 encodes an ortholog to neuropeptide Y receptors, which are reported to regulate feeding behavior in fishes, birds, and mammals.
source: It would also be consistent with the role of orthologs of npr-1 in other species. npr-1 encodes an ortholog to neuropeptide Y receptors, which are reported to regulate feeding behavior in fishes, birds, and mammals (Ando et al., 2001; Lecklin et al., 2002; Matsuda, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Ando et al., 2001; Lecklin et al., 2002; Matsuda, 2009.

claim: N2 animals cleared bacteria faster than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals in liquid media.
source: In these conditions, N2 cleared the bacteria faster than N2glb-5, npr-1 animals (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6b.

claim: N2 consumed more food than N2glb-5, npr-1 in both 10% and 21% environmental O2 conditions on agar plates.
source: When we tested N2 and N2glb-5, npr-1 animals in 10% or 21% environmental O2 levels, we found N2 consumed more food than N2glb-5, npr-1 in both environmental conditions (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6d.

claim: Animals grown in 10% O2 consume more food than animals grown in 21% O2.
source: Interestingly, we found animals grown in 10% O2 also consume more food than animals grown in 21% O2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on food consumption assays shown in Figure 6d.

claim: The N2 region surrounding npr-1 conferred a fitness advantage in the CB4856 background.
source: We found that the N2 region surrounding npr-1 also conferred a fitness advantage in the CB4856 background (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6f.

claim: The estimated selective coefficient of the derived allele of npr-1 was higher in the CB4856 background than the N2 background (s = 0.61 vs s = 0.30).
source: The estimated selective coefficients of the derived allele of npr-1 was higher in the CB4856 background than the N2 background (s = 0.61 vs s = 0.30), potentially due to the lower relative fitness of the CB4856 strain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on competition experiments.

claim: The derived allele of npr-1 increased food consumption in both N2 and CB4856 genetic backgrounds but its effect was higher in CB4856.
source: The derived allele of npr-1 increased food consumption in both genetic backgrounds but its effect was higher in CB4856.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6g.

claim: The effects of the derived allele of npr-1 on pharyngeal pumping rate was epistatic with respect to the N2 or CB4856 background.
source: The effects of the derived allele of npr-1 was epistatic with respect to the N2 or CB4856 background.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on pharyngeal pumping measurements shown in Figure 6h.

claim: The derived allele of npr-1 decreased the pumping rate in the CB4856 background but had no effect in the N2 background.
source: The derived allele decreased the pumping rate in the CB4856 background but had no effect in the N2 background (Figure 6h).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6h.

claim: Increased pharyngeal pumping does not necessarily lead to increases in food consumption.
source: Pumping rate is often used as a proxy for food consumption; our results indicate that increased pharyngeal pumping does not necessarily lead to increases in food consumption.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the pumping and food consumption data.

claim: glb-5 tunes O2-sensitivities of the URX oxygen-sensing neuron pair through regulation of O2-sensing guanylyl cyclases, leading to changes in influx of Ca++ into the cell body.
source: glb-5 tunes O2-sensititivies of the URX oxygen-sensing neuron pair through regulation of O2-sensing guanylyl cyclases, leading to changes in influx of Ca++ into the cell body (Abergel et al., 2016; Gross et al., 2014; McGrath et al., 2009; Oda et al., 2017; Persson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Abergel et al., 2016; Gross et al., 2014; McGrath et al., 2009; Oda et al., 2017; Persson et al., 2009.

claim: The derived allele of npr-1 inhibits the activity of the RMG hub interneuron which suppresses aerotaxis and social behavior.
source: The derived allele of npr-1 inhibits the activity of the RMG hub interneuron which suppresses aerotaxis and social behavior (Laurent et al., 2015; Macosko et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Laurent et al., 2015; Macosko et al., 2009.

claim: The RMG neurons connect to URX and a number of other sensory neurons through gap junctions, which are necessary for foraging behaviors.
source: The RMG neurons connect to URX and a number of other sensory neurons through gap junctions, which are necessary for foraging behaviors (Jang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Jang et al., 2017.

claim: URX neurons integrate O2 with internal nutrient reserves.
source: URX neurons also integrate O2 with internal nutrient reserves (Witham et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Witham et al., 2016.

claim: The relative fitness gains of the derived alleles were decreased by ablation of URX, AQR and PQR neurons.
source: In all cases, the relative fitness gains of the derived alleles were decreased by the presence of the neuronal ablation (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7b.

claim: Strains that carried the qaIs2241 cassette (ablating URX, AQR, PQR) were dramatically less fit than the control worms.
source: Strains that carried the qaIs2241 cassette were dramatically less fit than the control worms, suggesting that URX, AQR, and PQR promote fitness in laboratory conditions (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7c.

claim: URX, AQR, and PQR promote fitness in laboratory conditions.
source: Strains that carried the qaIs2241 cassette were dramatically less fit than the control worms, suggesting that URX, AQR, and PQR promote fitness in laboratory conditions (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7c.

claim: URX, AQR, and PQR neurons are required for social behaviors, food consumption and reproductive timing.
source: To test this, we phenotyped strains that carried the qaIs2241 cassette for social behaviors, food consumption and reproductive timing (Figure 7d–g). These experiments indicated that these neurons are required for each of these three traits.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7d-g.

claim: Food consumption in the qaIs2241 strains was reduced without a corresponding change in pharyngeal pumping rate.
source: Interestingly, food consumption in the qaIs2241 strains was reduced without a corresponding change in pharyngeal pumping rate, further confirming that these phenotypes could be separated from each other at a genetic and cellular level.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on data in Figure 7e and 7f.

claim: daf-22 was necessary for the fitness advantage of derived npr-1 and glb-5 alleles.
source: Competition experiments demonstrated that daf-22 was necessary for the fitness advantage of derived npr-1 and glb-5 alleles (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 8a.

claim: daf-22 was necessary for the faster sexual maturity of the N2 strain compared to N2glb-5,npr-1.
source: In addition, daf-22 was necessary for the faster sexual maturity (Figure 8b) and increased food intake (Figure 8c) of the N2 strain compared to N2glb-5,npr-1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 8b.

claim: daf-22 was necessary for the increased food intake of the N2 strain compared to N2glb-5,npr-1.
source: In addition, daf-22 was necessary for the faster sexual maturity (Figure 8b) and increased food intake (Figure 8c) of the N2 strain compared to N2glb-5,npr-1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 8c.

claim: npr-1 and glb-5 reprogram pheromone responses resulting in increased sexual maturity and ability to consume food.
source: These data suggest that npr-1 and glb-5 reprogram pheromone responses resulting in increased sexual maturity and ability to consume food.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the daf-22 experiments.

claim: daf-22 encodes a peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidation enzyme.
source: daf-22 encodes a peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidation enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as established knowledge.

claim: daf-22 plays a distinct role in ASK neurons, where it is required for the metabolization of fatty acids that stimulate the endoplasmic reticulum stress response, promoting the transcription of insulin-like peptides that regulate dauer formation and other biological processes.
source: Besides its role in the biosynthesis of ascaroside pheromones, daf-22 has recently been shown to play a distinct role in ASK neurons, where it is required for the metabolization of fatty acids that stimulate the endoplasmic reticulum stress response, promoting the transcription of insulin-like peptides that regulate dauer formation and other biological processes (Park and Paik, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to Park and Paik, 2017.

claim: daf-22 mutants accumulate massive amounts of fatty acids and fatty acyl-CoAs in their intestines.
source: daf-22 mutants also accumulate massive amounts of fatty acids and fatty acyl-CoAs in their intestines (Butcher et al., 2009; Joo et al., 2009; Li et al., 2016), which can potentially regulate feeding behavior through homeostasis mechanisms (Hyun et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to Butcher et al., 2009; Joo et al., 2009; Li et al., 2016.

claim: Neither of two concentrations of crude pheromone were able to rescue the differences in food consumption or reproductive timing in daf-22 mutants.
source: Neither of these concentrations were able to rescue the differences in food consumption or reproductive timing (Figure 8d,e).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 8d and 8e.

claim: The effects of the daf-22 mutants might be independent of their role in producing ascaroside pheromones.
source: These experiments suggest that the effects of the daf-22 mutants we have observed might be independent of their role in producing ascaroside pheromones.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the rescue experiments.

claim: Both alleles (npr-1 and glb-5) can be adaptive, with selective coefficients that are larger than many characterized beneficial alleles from other species.
source: We find that both alleles can be adaptive, with selective coefficients that are larger than many characterized beneficial alleles from other species.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a summary of findings.

claim: If the derived alleles spread through positive selection, it would suggest that the derived allele of npr-1 arose first, as the derived glb-5 allele is only beneficial in this derived genetic background.
source: These results are consistent with the derived alleles spreading through the ancestral N2 populations due to positive selection. If this was true, it would suggest that the derived allele of npr-1 arose first, as the derived glb-5 allele is only beneficial in this derived genetic background.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as an inference from the epistasis results.

claim: During the outcrossing phase of RIL construction, the N2 allele of npr-1 spread through the population to fixation, consistent with its dominant action and the strong selective advantage of this allele.
source: A recent example is provided by Noble and colleagues, who created a large mapping population between 16 parental strains (including N2 and CB4856) to create a large panel recombinant inbred lines (RILs) (Noble et al., 2017). During the outcrossing phase of construction, the N2 allele of npr-1 spread through the population to fixation, consistent with its dominant action and the strong selective advantage of this allele.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Noble et al., 2017.

claim: An excess of CB4856 haplotypes was observed in the RILs, suggesting that CB4856 haplotypes were more likely to contain beneficial alleles.
source: For example, an excess of CB4856 haplotypes was observed in the RILs, suggesting that CB4856 haplotypes were more likely to contain beneficial alleles.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as an observation from Noble et al., 2017.

claim: Epistatic interactions between CB4856 alleles and the derived allele of npr-1 could help resolve the paradox of CB4856's low fitness but excess haplotypes in RILs.
source: Potentially, epistatic interactions between CB4856 alleles and the derived allele of npr-1 could help resolve this; the effect of npr-1 on food intake and fitness is higher in the CB4856 background (Figure 6f,g).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a speculation to explain observations.

claim: Differences in effect size of a focal allele in different genetic backgrounds is considered evidence for the existence of epistasis.
source: Differences in effect size of a focal allele in different genetic backgrounds is considered evidence for the existence of epistasis (Gibson and Dworkin, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Gibson and Dworkin, 2004.

claim: The social/solitary feeding behavioral changes of N2 are not sufficient for explaining its fitness gains.
source: However, our work suggests that the social/solitary feeding behavioral changes of N2 are not sufficient for explaining its fitness gains.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Changes to food intake, sexual maturity, and fecundity are more important for fitness gains than social/solitary behavioral changes.
source: Rather, we propose that changes to food intake, sexual maturity, and fecundity are more important.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: There must be some sort of tradeoff – either energetically or developmentally – that makes the derived mutation unfavorable in natural environments.
source: One unresolved question is why wild strains do not eat as much food as the N2 strain. We believe there must be some sort of tradeoff – either energetically or developmentally – that makes the derived mutation unfavorable in their natural environments.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a speculation about evolutionary constraints.

claim: URX could regulate food consumption indirectly by stimulating metabolism of fatty acids.
source: Alternatively, URX could regulate food consumption indirectly by stimulating metabolism of fatty acids.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a speculation about mechanisms.

claim: URX neurons monitor fat stores, which are thought to regulate tonic Ca++ responses of the URX neurons.
source: URX, along with AQR and PQR, are body cavity neurons, sending ciliated dendrites into the coelomic fluid, which serves as the circulatory system for C. elegans (White et al., 1986). Besides sensing external O2, URX neurons monitor fat stores, which are thought to regulate tonic Ca++ responses of the URX neurons (Witham et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with citations to White et al., 1986 and Witham et al., 2016.

claim: URX can stimulate fat loss, creating a homeostatic loop that ensures that fat mobilization only occurs when there are sufficient fat reserves and when environmental O2 is high enough to metabolize the fatty acids into energy.
source: URX, in turn, can stimulate fat loss, creating a homeostatic loop that ensures that fat mobilization only occurs when there are sufficient fat reserves and when environmental O2 is high enough to metabolize the fatty acids into energy (Witham et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Witham et al., 2016.

claim: Fat metabolism has been shown to regulate satiety behavior in C. elegans.
source: Fat metabolism has been shown to regulate satiety behavior in C. elegans, which could account for increases in food consumption we see in these strains (Hyun et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Hyun et al., 2016.

claim: Primer pheromones have been shown to influence body fat metabolism in C. elegans through the ADL sensory neuron.
source: Primer pheromones have been shown to influence body fat metabolism in C. elegans through the ADL sensory neuron (Hussey et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Hussey et al., 2017.

claim: ADL sensory neurons are regulated by pheromones in an npr-1-dependent manner.
source: ADL sensory neurons are regulated by pheromones in an npr-1-dependent manner (Abergel et al., 2016; Fenk and de Bono, 2017; Jang et al., 2012; Jang et al., 2017; Macosko et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with citations to Abergel et al., 2016; Fenk and de Bono, 2017; Jang et al., 2012; Jang et al., 2017; Macosko et al., 2009.

claim: There is a large difference in relative fitness between different strains of C. elegans when competed in the laboratory.
source: Despite the attempts of researchers to create fertile conditions for nematodes to grow in, we found a large difference in relative fitness between different strains of C. elegans when competed in the laboratory.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a summary of findings.

claim: Natural genetic variation and de novo variation both result in fitness differences that selection can act on.
source: Natural genetic variation and de novo variation both result in fitness differences that selection can act on.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a general principle.

claim: The laboratory selection pressures characterized in this study will generalize to other invertebrate and vertebrate animals.
source: We believe that the laboratory selection pressures we characterized here will generalize to other invertebrate and vertebrate animals.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a speculation about broader implications.

claim: Not only will the traits that confer fitness advantages be modified in laboratory animals, but potentially additional traits due to the pleiotropic actions of many genes, and relaxed stabilizing selection on traits in laboratory conditions.
source: Our work suggests that not only will the traits that confer fitness advantages be modified, but potentially additional traits due to the pleiotropic actions of many genes, and relaxed stabilizing selection on traits in laboratory conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a conclusion about laboratory adaptation.
